small_guidance:
- Add channels-tiled K-loop accumulation (BLOCK_IC tile, e.g. 4 or 8) and use `tl.dot` on a [BLOCK_N, BLOCK_IC] × [BLOCK_IC, BLOCK_OC] tile per (kh,kw) — current code does pure outer-products which under-utilizes tensor cores. With IC=8, a single BLOCK_IC=8 tile covers the channel dim per kh/kw.
- Tile the spatial output as 2D (BLOCK_OH × BLOCK_OW) instead of flattened BLOCK_N so consecutive `ow` lanes share the same `ih` row — input loads coalesce on W and weight loads can be hoisted out of the ow dimension. Try BLOCK_OH=8, BLOCK_OW=32, BLOCK_OC=64, num_warps=4.
- Add autotune configs with larger BLOCK_OC (up to 64 since OC=64 fits exactly) and drop the BLOCK_OC=128 config (it wastes half the lanes); also try num_stages=4 with BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_OC=64.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an implicit-GEMM where each program computes a [BLOCK_M_OC × BLOCK_N_SPATIAL] output tile via `tl.dot`, with the K dimension being IC*KH*KW=72. Pad K to a multiple of 16 and run a single inner loop with `tl.dot` so tensor cores are engaged — this is the main missing factor vs. the current outer-product accumulator.
- Use NHWC (channels-last) input layout: permute x once at forward entry (or have ModelNew store weight in a reshaped [OC, KH, KW, IC] layout) so the GEMM-K stride is contiguous and a single vectorized `tl.load` fetches BLOCK_K channels.
- Persist the weight tile in registers/SMEM by making each program own a full BLOCK_OC slice and stream output spatial tiles through it (persistent kernel over spatial, loop over output tiles inside the program), amortizing weight loads across many spatial tiles. Fuse ReLU+HardSwish in the epilogue exactly as today.
